brief: Goldman macro strategists Shah and Codacci-Pisanelli run three chains. Crude upside is capped because dark transits rose and Chinese crude buying is price elastic, with Persian Gulf exports at 15-16mb/day or two thirds of pre-war levels, so Brent can hold its recent range. Products do not. European gas sits near the highs and diesel is more stressed, which is what gets consumed, and the open question is whether that spills into core inflation. Front end UK and European rates now trade closer to natgas than crude and are hard to trade. Second, Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech lowered the CPI strike that would warrant a September hike, and Waller's pushback on disinflation, non-market services prices, fading tariffs and a PCE methodology change worth a few tenths puts him at a hold absent a hot print. CPI next week decides, a 0.2 MoM core print holds, and any hiking cycle would be shallow, though a couple of hikes might still help Warsh's credibility and the long end. Third, WAM reduction, buybacks and tightening flatten curves without fixing large deficits meeting lower duration demand, so outright long end yields keep making new highs and European long end stays their short.
